title: The Innovation SSI-2001's SID register window
covers: the 32-byte window of the Innovation SSI-2001, as the MOS 6581 manual maps its registers and DOSBox-X handles each offset

rows.text: The two registers together form the 16-bit number that sets oscillator 1's frequency.
The low register and the high register are the low and high halves of that 16-bit number.
The handler enables the mixer channel when the last use is zero and records the current tick count.
The read handler answers with the SID's read of the register's offset.
The two registers form the 12-bit number that sets the duty cycle of oscillator 1's pulse waveform.
Bits 4-7 of the high register are not used, so a write carries twelve bits of the number.
The handler enables the mixer channel when the last use is zero and records the current tick count.
The read handler answers with the SID's read of the register's offset.
The register holds eight control bits that select options on oscillator 1.
Bits 4-7 are stored as a four-bit waveform selection, one bit each for triangle, sawtooth, pulse and noise.
The register stores bit 0 as GATE, which starts the envelope's attack and decay and, cleared, its release.
The register stores bit 1 as SYNC, which the document says synchronizes oscillator 1 with oscillator 3.
The register stores bit 2 as RING MOD, which the document says combines oscillators 1 and 3.
The register stores bit 3 as TEST; a write with the bit set resets oscillator 1 at zero and resets the noise output.
The programmer should select a waveform to hear the voice, and be careful when selecting several together.
The handler enables the mixer channel when the last use is zero and records the current tick count.
The read handler answers with the SID's read of the register's offset.
Bits 4-7 select one of sixteen attack rates and bits 0-3 one of sixteen decay rates for voice 1.
A write carries the attack rate in its high nibble and the decay rate in its low nibble.
The handler enables the mixer channel when the last use is zero and records the current tick count.
The read handler answers with the SID's read of the register's offset.
Bits 4-7 select one of sixteen sustain levels and bits 0-3 one of sixteen release rates for voice 1.
A write carries the sustain level in its high nibble and the release rate in its low nibble.
The handler enables the mixer channel when the last use is zero and records the current tick count.
The read handler answers with the SID's read of the register's offset.
Registers 07h-0Dh control voice 2 and are functionally identical to registers 00h-06h, except for the SYNC and RING MOD source it names.
07h and 08h are voice 2's frequency low and high bytes.
09h and 0Ah are voice 2's pulse width low and high bytes.
0Bh is voice 2's control register; the document routes its SYNC to oscillator 1 and its RING MOD to oscillators 2 and 1.
0Ch carries voice 2's attack and decay rates.
0Dh carries voice 2's sustain level and release rate.
The handler enables the mixer channel when the last use is zero and records the current tick count.
The read handler answers with the SID's read of the register's offset.
Registers 0Eh-14h control voice 3 and are functionally identical to registers 00h-06h, except for the SYNC and RING MOD source it names.
0Eh and 0Fh are voice 3's counterparts of 00h and 01h, its frequency low and high bytes.
10h and 11h are voice 3's counterparts of 02h and 03h, its pulse width low and high bytes.
12h is voice 3's counterpart of 04h, its control register; the document routes its SYNC to oscillator 2 and its RING MOD to oscillators 3 and 2.
13h is voice 3's counterpart of 05h, its attack and decay rates.
14h is voice 3's counterpart of 06h, its sustain level and release rate.
Typical operation selects frequency, waveform and envelope rates, then gates the voice; voices can also be used in unison.
The handler enables the mixer channel when the last use is zero and records the current tick count.
The read handler answers with the SID's read of the register's offset.
The two registers form the 11-bit number that sets the filter's cutoff frequency.
Bits 3-7 of the low register are not used, so a write carries eleven bits of the number.
The handler enables the mixer channel when the last use is zero and records the current tick count.
The read handler answers with the SID's read of the register's offset.
Bits 4-7 set the resonance, and bits 0-3 route voices 1, 2 and 3 and the external input through the filter.
A write stores its high nibble as the resonance and its low nibble as the filter routing.
The handler enables the mixer channel when the last use is zero and records the current tick count.
The read handler answers with the SID's read of the register's offset.
Bits 4-7 select the filter mode and output options; bits 0-3 set the output volume.
A write stores bits 0-3 as the volume, bits 4-6 as the filter mode and bit 7 as voice 3 off.
The handler enables the mixer channel when the last use is zero and records the current tick count.
The read handler answers with the SID's read of the register's offset.
The register lets the processor read the potentiometer tied to POTX, from 0 at minimum resistance to 255 at maximum.
The value is always valid and is updated every 512 clock cycles.
A read returns 0xff always: the potentiometer is not modeled, so the value never changes.
The handler enables the mixer channel when the last use is zero and records the current tick count.
The read handler answers with the SID's read of the register's offset.
The register lets the processor read the potentiometer tied to POTY.
Same as POTX, for the potentiometer tied to POTY.
A read returns 0xff always: the potentiometer is not modeled, so the value never changes.
The handler enables the mixer channel when the last use is zero and records the current tick count.
The read handler answers with the SID's read of the register's offset.
The register lets the processor read the upper eight output bits of oscillator 3.
The register returns the upper eight bits of oscillator 3's output.
The programmer can use the register as a random number generator, because the noise waveform gives random numbers.
The handler enables the mixer channel when the last use is zero and records the current tick count.
The read handler answers with the SID's read of the register's offset.
Register $1C is ENV 3, which lets the processor read the voice 3 envelope generator's output.
The programmer can add this output to the filter frequency for harmonic envelopes and WAH, or to an oscillator's frequency control for phaser sounds.
A read returns the voice 3 envelope generator's output.
The envelope generator must be gated for this register to produce any output.
The OSC 3 register always reflects the oscillator's changing output, which the envelope generator does not affect.
The handler enables the mixer channel when the last use is zero and records the current tick count.
The read handler answers with the SID's read of the register's offset.
A write stores the byte as the bus value; the write switch's default arm changes no register.

searched.gave: MAME's mos6581 device cites no document in its header, and MAME has no Innovation SSI-2001 board.
The maker's October 1982 preliminary datasheet is the only SID document found.
No 6581 datasheet: the mos_technology listing refused an automated request (HTTP 403) and a site search found none.
The October 1982 preliminary datasheet scan the dictionary uses, mos_6581_sid_preliminary_october_1982.
datasheetarchive.com lists a 6581 scan; cpcwiki and 6502.org hold copies of the same datasheet.

rows.text: Offsets 0x1D to 0x1F are not among the read switch's cases: the default returns the bus byte.
A read returns the last byte written to any SID register, or 0 once its 0x2000-cycle age runs out.
A write stores the byte as the bus value; the write switch's default arm changes no register.
The handler enables the mixer channel when the last use is zero and records the current tick count.
The read handler answers with the SID's read of the register's offset.
